messages:
Ravi P.: FYI: Platform will replace long-lived CI tokens and unsigned Jira webhooks with our OIDC broker + signed webhooks. Pilot week starts 2026-05-04, opt-in May 11-25, enforcement May 26.

Lina M.: Clarify: repo vs org scope?

Ravi P.: Both. Ingress will validate JWTs for webhooks and only accept ephemeral OIDC creds for CI jobs. Well provide compatibility headers for two weeks after enforcement.

Tom S.: Will terraform-managed endpoints break?

Ravi P.: Not immediately. Update manifests to include `webhook_owner` and the new `jira.webhook_secret` resource. See docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/platform/jira-webhooks.

Maya (sec): Security note: all managed vendor secrets will be rotated automatically. Self-managed endpoints must rotate by May 20 or deliveries stop. Exceptions require a ticket.

Infra-bot: Inventory scan scheduled May 1-3. Teams: update service manifests before May 3.

Lina M.: How to test locally?

Ravi P.: Use the local harness: start the ingress and sign payloads with scripts/sign_webhook.py, or run `make run-local-ingress`. We also published `rw-webhook-migrate` and `rw-oidc-attach` CLIs for bulk updates.

Tom S.: Rollback plan?

Ravi P.: Ingress will have permissive mode that logs verification failures but accepts requests for 48h after each batch. We can flip back legacy auth for specific endpoints via feature flag if needed.

Maya (sec): New alerts: >10 signature failures/min triggers a P2. Also enforcing HSTS/strict TLS; file a ticket if you use non-ACME certs.

Lina M.: How to join pilot?

Ravi P.: Sign up: https://go.redwood.dev/jira-webhook-pilot by Apr 28. Prioritizing customer-facing and high-traffic services.

Tom S.: We'll add `ingress` and `webhook-proxy`.

Ravi P.: Thanks — posting a short how-to and rollout batches later. Ping Maya for exceptions with delivery IDs. :white_check_mark:
